title: Bookmark object_id cannot represent BigAutoField primary keys
reasoning: Article, Video, and Recipe all use BigAutoField primary keys, but Bookmark stores the generic target ID in a PositiveIntegerField. On databases such as PostgreSQL this is a 32-bit integer with a maximum of 2147483647, while BigAutoField is 64-bit. Once a learning resource row ID exceeds the 32-bit range, creating a bookmark for it will fail or be impossible, breaking the bookmark contract for valid target objects.
recommendation: Change Bookmark.object_id to models.PositiveBigIntegerField, or to a CharField if bookmarks are intended to support arbitrary content types with non-integer primary keys. Add a migration that alters the column type without narrowing existing values.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for migrations or bookmark behavior, and typical fixtures create small IDs that would not expose the 32-bit overflow boundary.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a migration/model test that creates or simulates a target object with an ID greater than 2147483647 and verifies a Bookmark can be saved for it.
minimumFixScope: Alter learning_resources Bookmark.object_id to a 64-bit-compatible field and generate the corresponding migration.
